text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Six leaders of opposition FORD-Kenya party declare the quest for a single opposition candidate dead and announce the formation of a new pressure group that will mobilise Kenyans to seek more political changes before the general elections.
- At least 80 members of the Kenya Human Rights Commission hold a demonstration in Nairobi carrying the coffin of a woman shot dead by police 13 days ago.
- A mother of two, presumed dead and buried six months ago shocks relatives and friends when she resurfaces.
- The on-going investigation into the mysterious death of University of Nairobi student leader Solomon Muruli takes a new twist after the police pick up Muruli's younger sister for blood tests.
- Langata Member of Parliament Raila Odinga accuses the Kenyan press of biased reporting.
- A Nairobi court hears how 60 people who have sued the ruling party have no legal rights as they are bogus party members.
- The Roman Catholic Church says there is no evidence that the ruling party is using relief food as a campaign tool for the forthcoming general election.
- Belligerent Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru cuts short his official visit to Europe.
- The attorney general's office is in a major crisis after being taken for a very expensive ride by expatriate lawyers who have quit their jobs and secretly sold government-owned furniture.

- The government orders state-run Kenya Broadcasting Corporation (KBC) radio not to broadcast Raila Odinga's win in the Langata constituency by-election again after reading them out once in the early morning bulletin.
- As the war in Eastern Zaire intensifies, KBC appears to have blanked out clips from the region especially those in favour of rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
